title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-04-04
lineage: MSR > C > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a fiery 1969 set with a smoking Other One slide and powerful Dark Star, though occasional hiss and uneven moments temper the experience.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers clear, punchy soundboard detail—snare hits are audible and early songs like Schoolgirl and Feedback ring sweet—but a noticeable hiss and drop‑outs around the drum solo and Death Don't detract from the listening flow. Musically the show shines on The Other One (Jerry’s slide is called "sick"), Dark Star, Too, Eleven and the feedback climax, while Lovelight and an uninspired Schoolgirl fall flat and the keyboards (TC) are widely criticized.

ai_rating.rationale: Majority of reviewers rate 5 stars, praising the performance and many aspects of the sound; a handful note hiss, drop‑outs, and weak songs, pulling the overall average to about 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early portion is crisp and clear with excellent snare detail; several reviewers note minimal hiss but others report noticeable hiss and deterioration around the drum solo and Death Don't, plus occasional drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as dynamite with strong openings; second set starts oddly with a lengthy Lovelight that drags, but picks up with an intense Dark Star/Stephen/Eleven/Feedback sequence and a fast‑paced Eleven finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Slide work on The Other One repeatedly called "sick"; aggressive, fiery playing throughout, though some reviewers note occasional abrupt quits mid‑jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Generally praised for solid bass foundation and “great” sound, especially in heavy jams like Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Bob: Impressive rhythm guitar noted as a highlight by several listeners.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) heavily criticized—described as terrible, awful, and out of tune, particularly on Lovelight and early set portions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Snare detail praised for clarity; however hiss and sound deterioration around the drum solo were mentioned, and Mickey’s cowbell usage drew criticism.
